preparation_independence: Prepared from pinned normative AC-10/GO-I1/GO-I3/GO-I7 and observed publication boundaries before consuming any executable S2/S3 integrated candidate.
shared_preconditions: S1 frozen scope, compatible-producer/contract identities and admitted allocation
S2 exact producer/corpus/recipe and S3 exact generation/recovery candidate
S5 single integrated commit plus hashes of every consumed dependency
Isolated target with existing policy/authority, no production writes or authority fabrication
Known-good published predecessor and independent scope before mutation
Permitted CI runner for product tests; local inspection does not substitute for it

cases.setup: Begin with an accepted current predecessor; prepare a complete reviewed candidate through S2/S3 without activation.
cases.expected: Preparation may create private CAS/candidate objects, but all current readers remain bound to the previous still-valid accepted manifest or return the contract's HOLD; no reader serves the unactivated candidate.
cases.positive_control: Read the current accepted predecessor before staging and identify its exact body/result/receipt bytes.
cases.forbidden_substitute: Treating candidate existence or CAS put as publication.
cases.blocker: Exact integrated candidate and isolated target unavailable.

cases.setup: Use the same complete candidate first without required ratification and then with separately existing authorized isolated-target credentials.
cases.expected: Unauthorized attempt does not emit and leaves current authority unchanged. Authorized isolated activation emits only if all source/attachment/authz/ratify gates pass; readback serves exactly that accepted candidate.
cases.positive_control: The authorized attempt must exercise the same caller and source-bound candidate; credential authority must be evidenced independently.
cases.forbidden_substitute: Creating a permissive policy, substituting historical reviewer IDs or forging a ratification token.
cases.blocker: S2/S3 candidate, exact new review binding and isolated authority absent.

cases.setup: Fix old implementation bytes and the new accepted scope/producer contract, then invoke the actual old publishing path against that isolated target.
cases.expected: The old producer cannot change the accepted new-scope publication; capture actual caller, version, emitted/refused result and current reader identity afterward. The reason must be the real applicable compatibility/authority refusal, not a new label asserted by the test author.
cases.positive_control: The contract-approved new producer can publish a compatible candidate under equivalent valid authority.
cases.forbidden_substitute: Calling a fixed-scope pilot on mismatched data, withholding a generic token, comparing lexicographic SHAs, or adding the historical 87abf90956 mismatch guard.
cases.blocker: No observed rule yet distinguishes admissible new producer from retained old producer for the new accepted scope.

cases.setup: Change the recipe under the applicable new contract, recapture inputs, rebuild affected results and obtain fresh exact reviews.
cases.expected: A genuinely compatible reviewed update is not refused solely because its recipeVersion differs from the previous receipt. The new recipe identity and dependencies are bound in the new receipt.
cases.positive_control: Retain the valid RB-07 recipe-a-2/RB-11 recipe-b-2 update shapes as regression obligations; their historical assertions are not new execution evidence.
cases.forbidden_substitute: Treating arbitrary version strings or commit SHAs as a chronological compatibility order.
cases.blocker: Recipe/producer compatibility contract and candidate unavailable.

cases.setup: Preserve the previous accepted manifest and all dependencies; prove that target sources, registered membership, contract, recipe and trust remain compatible before rollback.
cases.expected: Only an explicitly compatible predecessor may become current. Reopened readers return its exact accepted bytes and version bindings; unrelated valid scope remains usable.
cases.positive_control: Read the accepted predecessor and successor before rollback; capture the compatibility tuple used by the actual reader.
cases.forbidden_substitute: Copying an older sidecar or citing an old accepted manifest without checking current source/contract compatibility.
cases.blocker: S3 rollback path and an exact compatible target snapshot have not been supplied.

cases.setup: Retain source or contract drift while attempting to reuse the accepted predecessor as current; keep a separate valid scope unchanged.
cases.expected: The attempted current publication/read holds with the observed incompatibility reason. The current-source requirement is not satisfied by historical acceptance. No stale body is returned as current.
cases.positive_control: The same predecessor is readable as current only in a separate state whose compatibility tuple actually matches.
cases.forbidden_substitute: Restoring source bytes silently, relabelling stale bytes as current or dropping the new contract requirement.
cases.blocker: Exact drifted candidate state and runner unavailable.

cases.clause: explicit historical read preserves trust and label
cases.setup: Use a retained accepted predecessor with current-input drift and otherwise valid trust; separately exercise untrusted state.
cases.expected: Any allowed historical response names its original identities and historical=true. Historical mode never authorizes untrusted bytes, bypasses missing objects or silently becomes current.
cases.positive_control: A valid current read carries the current candidate identities, with historical mode not silently requested.
cases.forbidden_substitute: Serving a raw CAS/body path after the governed reader returned HOLD.
cases.blocker: Exact published manifests and trust states missing.

cases.clause: foreign-identity replacement refusal preserves readable prior projection
cases.setup: Attempt a foreign-identity replacement through the real governed path while the incumbent store remains trusted and complete.
cases.expected: The replacement is refused and reopening returns the previously accepted projection, with byte-identical protected objects.
cases.positive_control: A valid same-target replacement is allowed only through normal authority and complete generation validation.
cases.forbidden_substitute: Treating an untrusted incumbent store as a guaranteed readable preserved generation.
cases.blocker: S3 integrated candidate unavailable; existing G3-03 citation is not rerun or generalized.

cases.clause: untrusted incumbent refuses without sidecar fallback
cases.setup: Break trust in the isolated store without substituting the store implementation or forcing a mocked get result.
cases.expected: Read/publication refuses according to the real trust boundary; capture the actual result. The prior bytes remain protected evidence but are not served merely because they still exist on disk.
cases.positive_control: Before the mutation, the exact store is trusted and the expected current generation is readable.
cases.forbidden_substitute: Untrusted sidecar fallback or manufacturing ownership-integrity via a stubbed DiskStore.get.
cases.blocker: No executable candidate/isolated trust fixture and permitted runner.

cases.setup: Freeze the S1 protected set plus original sources/responses/claims/judgments/manifests and enumerate exact before-state bytes.
cases.expected: Every protected original retains its bytes at each stage. Authorized new outputs receive new identities and preserve predecessor links; no old failure, response, review, artifact or source identity is rewritten.
cases.positive_control: The 88 historical files/62 declared pins and original artifact subsets already byte-verified form reusable preparation evidence, but the runtime sequence still needs its own state snapshots.
cases.forbidden_substitute: Replacing the migration comparison with a Git-only diff or the existence of an old backup.
cases.blocker: S1 complete set and actual integrated runtime sequence absent.

cases.clause: unrelated accepted scope remains usable across migration
cases.setup: Keep an independently valid scope with distinct required closure and capture its result/receipt/body before changing the migrating scope.
cases.expected: All observations preserve readability and exact identities of the independent scope, except when the specifically tested shared dependency/manifest is itself corrupted; that is a separate shared-corruption case.
cases.positive_control: Both scopes start readable through the real host entry points.
cases.forbidden_substitute: Assuming directory separation proves closure independence or counting successful low-level reads as host wiring.
cases.blocker: S1 scope graph and S2/S3 exact manifests absent.

cases.setup: Identify any generated public/boundary surface actually changed by S5 integration and invoke its owning generator on the exact candidate.
cases.expected: Generated bytes correspond to the generator's source and remain compatible with readers/consumers; record command, source hashes, runner and resulting diff. Unchanged surfaces may be reported as unchanged only after exact diff.
cases.positive_control: Existing byte-reproduction checks remain in the selected CI scope; no manual generated edit supplies the expected output.
cases.forbidden_substitute: Calling a source citation a generator execution or inventing a claim that manual edits are physically impossible.
cases.blocker: No integrated candidate delta or applicable generated gate result.
